Where we scoop in Citrus Park.

Citrus Park sits between Perryville Road and Cotton Lane, from Northern Avenue south to about Camelback Road. About 5,200 people live there. It is not part of any city, and its mail comes through the Waddell post office. We scoop all of Citrus Park and the homes next to it, like Zanjero Trails.

We scoop inside the orange line. That includes the homes in between, like Zanjero Trails.

Why Citrus Park yards need weekly pickup.

Big lots and green grass. Many Citrus Park homes sit on an acre or more with flood irrigation, so the grass stays green. Thick grass hides poop, and dogs have lots of room to roam. That makes piles easy to miss.

Monsoon storms spread it. From mid June through September, heavy rain can wash poop into the street. Maricopa County says storm drain water goes to rivers and lakes without being treated.

Heat and flies. Phoenix has a normal July high of about 106 degrees. Heat makes poop smell stronger, and University of Arizona experts say flies breed in pet waste. Weekly pickup stops the smell before it starts.

Germs stay in the soil. The CDC says roundworm eggs from dog poop can live in soil for months or even years. Its advice is to pick up dog poop, even in your own yard, and most of all where kids play.
